questions.question: When you see a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon with two flashing red lights, what must you do?

options.text: Continue forward carefully.
Stop completely, then continue forward carefully.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then continue forward carefully.
questions.explanation: A Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon helps pedestrians cross safely. It only works when a pedestrian activates it. Two flashing red lights mean you must stop completely before going forward carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
Dangerous curve ahead.
Bump in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on yellow background. They tell drivers about upcoming dangers. This sign warns you that wet pavement can be slippery and hard to control.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will hit the curb and stop.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. The water brings oil from the pavement to the surface. This is even worse in hot weather when more oil rises to the road.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway, to enter or exit a highway, or to make a U-turn if permitted.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look, then go if there is no traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells drivers to slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get in a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: First, adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.

questions.question: What is most important about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your car's momentum makes it hard to turn. To keep control, you must slow down before entering a curve.

questions.question: Which one does NOT affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much you drink, how long between drinks, and your weight. Your level of fitness does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines. When can you cross them?

options.text: Only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
To pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Never.
Only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You can only cross them to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield
Do not enter

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down and let other traffic and pedestrians go first. Only stop if you must.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spots by:

options.text: Using the inside rearview mirror.
Using the outside rearview mirror.
Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before every lane change to check your blind spots.

questions.question: You come to an intersection that is blocked by other traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
Sound your horn to make the cars move up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if you cannot drive all the way through. Wait until the traffic ahead clears so you don't block the intersection.

questions.question: Allow a larger space cushion than usual when stopping:

options.text: On an incline.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On an incline.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, extra space reduces the chance of a collision.

questions.question: When a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System starts to lose traction on a slippery road, drivers should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press hard on the brake pedal and hold it steady while steering to safety. The ABS system will pump the brakes automatically faster than you can. Releasing pressure or pumping manually will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: It is illegal for a person 21 years of age or older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: For drivers age 21 and older, 0.08 percent BAC or higher is illegal. Driving under the influence is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection when the traffic light changes from green to solid yellow. You should:

options.text: Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop immediately.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through the intersection before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down and stop before entering the intersection when the light turns yellow, if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive carefully through.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:

options.text: Enter above the speed of traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Accelerate to the speed of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate to the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match traffic. Signal, find an opening, and merge smoothly into traffic at the same speed.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersections are coming up.
Road work ahead.
The road curves to the right.
Traffic lanes will change.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to go after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, look for a second train on the other track before you go.
Honk your horn when you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, look for a second train on the other track before you go.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks side by side, a second train may be coming on the other track after the first train passes. Wait until you are sure no trains are coming from either direction on either track before you cross.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and use your turn signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but traffic is heavy. You should:

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for that traffic to pass before you turn. You can enter the intersection to get ready for your left turn if the light is green and no other car is turning left in front of you.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. This means:

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You must turn left soon.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line at the road edge shows where the road boundary is. When the edge line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.
